# Trajectory-Derived Confidence for Reliable, Resource-Aware Clinical Text-to-SQL Agents

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#sentinel)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.04156v1) · arXiv:2610.04156v1, 2 October 2026; manuscript reports a Resource-Aware Agentic AI workshop

**Reading coverage:** All 19 pages, Sections 1-6, Appendices A-M, decision equations, Tables 1-9, figure captions, prompts and complete example trajectory.

## Research question

Clinical SQL agents can spend multiple steps producing plausible incorrect answers or answering questions unsupported by the database.

## Method

Two per-agent ModernBERT classifiers score question/trajectory prefixes for answerability and eventual correctness. Calibration selects early-exit thresholds and delivery-time Chow-style withholding, optionally combining transcript scores with execution/schema features.

## Evaluation

Five fixed ReAct agents on template-disjoint pools constructed from EHRSQL/MIMIC-III training and validation data. Primary correctness uses GPT-4o-mini judgments after strict mismatches; template-cluster intervals and strict-label sensitivity are reported.

## What the results support

At low error penalty the monitor improves utility over always abstaining for four of five agents while reducing coverage. At higher penalties results are statistically comparable to refusing everything. Early stopping saves agent steps, but reported savings exclude monitor inference overhead.

## Limits and qualifications

One database and mostly one seed; monitors need agent-specific trajectories. A human audit finds judge disagreement on 26% of adjudicated hard cases. Question-only shortcuts nearly solve answerability, and strict execution labels substantially reduce gains. No competing confidence implementation is evaluated.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Clarifies trade-offs among refusal, correctness, coverage and compute; benchmark utility is not evidence of safe clinical deployment.

## Checks against the paper

These are interpretations checked against the source, not verbatim quotations attributed to its authors.

| Claim or inference examined | Original evidence | Location | Assessment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sentinel yields reliable high-stakes answers. | Appendix F finds gains over always-refuse indistinguishable from zero at medium/high penalties; coverage is very low. | Table 1, Appendices E-F, Tables 3-4 | A useful abstention verdict rather than demonstrated high-coverage clinical reliability. |
| The confidence layer saves computation. | Table 2 and Appendix G count avoided agent steps/tokens; two ModernBERT passes per step are explicitly not subtracted. | Section 4.3/Table 2 and Appendix G | Gross agent-call savings, not measured net end-to-end resource savings. |
| Semantic scoring is unbiased. | Two authors agree on 93/100 selected hard cases; judge agrees on 69 of 93, with 11 false positives and 13 false negatives. | Appendix B | Near-balanced errors in this selected audit do not establish unbiasedness outside it; label uncertainty affects results. |
